name.text: Changing the Subject 4 - Put the steps in order (drag and drop)

questiontext.text:
A boda boda rider's speed is given by the formula \(v = u + at\), where \(v\) is the final speed, \(u\) is the starting speed, \(a\) is the acceleration and \(t\) is the time.

Starting from \(v = u + at\), make \(t\) the subject of the formula.

Drag the steps you need into the answer area and put them in the correct order.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] { "steps": {# parsons_encode(steps) #}, "headers": ["Your solution (in order):"], "available_header": "Steps to choose from:" } [[/parsons]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Step 1: subtract \(u\) from both sides. \(u\) is added to \(at\), so subtracting \(u\) removes it from the right-hand side:

\[ v - u = u + at - u \quad\Longrightarrow\quad v - u = at. \]

Step 2: divide both sides by \(a\). \(t\) is multiplied by \(a\), so dividing by \(a\) leaves \(t\) on its own. The whole left-hand side \(v - u\) is divided by \(a\), not just one term (we need \(a \neq 0\)):

\[ \dfrac{v - u}{a} = \dfrac{at}{a} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{v - u}{a} = t. \]

Step 3: rewrite with \(t\) on the left. Swapping the two sides does not change the equation, and it is usual to write the subject first:

\[ t = \dfrac{v - u}{a}. \]

The correct order is:

  1. Subtract \(u\) from both sides: \(v - u = at\)
  2. Divide both sides by \(a\): \(\dfrac{v - u}{a} = t\)
  3. Rewrite with \(t\) on the left: \(t = \dfrac{v - u}{a}\)

Why the other two steps are wrong.

  • "Add \(u\) to both sides: \(v + u = at\)". Adding \(u\) to the right-hand side gives \(u + at + u\), so \(u\) does not disappear. Moving \(u\) to the other side without changing its sign is a common mistake. To remove a term that is added, subtract it.
  • "Divide both sides by \(a\): \(\dfrac{v}{a} = u + t\)". Dividing the right-hand side by \(a\) gives \(\dfrac{u}{a} + t\), because every term must be divided, so \(u\) has been left undivided. Removing \(u\) first, by subtracting, avoids this.

node.description: Correct steps in the correct order
Used the "divide only part of the side by a" distractor?

truefeedback.text: One of your steps divides only part of the right-hand side by \(a\). When you divide one side of an equation by a number, every term on that side must be divided. While \(u\) is still added to \(at\), which operation should you undo first?

node.description: Used the "move u across without changing sign" distractor?

truefeedback.text: One of your steps adds \(u\) to both sides. Check what that does to the right-hand side: \(u + at + u\) still contains \(u\), so it hasn't been removed. To remove a term that is added, use the inverse operation.

node.description: Right steps, wrong order (otherwise: steps missing)?

truefeedback.text: You have chosen the right steps, but they are not in the right order. Look at the equation each step starts from. Undo the operations on \(t\) in the reverse order to the one they were applied in, and write the subject on the left at the end.

falsefeedback.text: Your solution is missing at least one step. Keep going until \(t\) is on its own and the formula is written in the form \(t = \dots\).
